title: A Blatant Tutorial
text: “The Naofumi-san from the first world seems like a difficult reference point for a lot of things, doesn’t he. We should probably just assume he developed some kind of flying magic through whatever means available.”
“That’s basically what Gaelion said too.”
“It’s me, sure, but my personality’s pretty different, so maybe I could manage it with enough effort—but let’s focus on what we can actually do right now instead.”
“Given that Naofumi-san’s a Peckul, it seems safe to assume he’d shine underwater.”
“Well, he’s a penguin, after all.”
At this point, Ren suddenly fell silent.
“Ren-san can’t swim, right? Seems safe to leave that department entirely to Naofumi-san then.”
“The problem is when it comes to stuff that can just be muscled through with brute force.”
Father looked over at me. Should you desire it, I shall handle it, I say.
“Motoyasu-san would probably split the sea open without batting an eye, and with some kind of Drive Mode, he could probably manage diving too.”
“At this rate can’t Motoyasu alone just handle everything by himself? His sense of smell’s probably on par with mine too.”
“If you say that, there’s no point to any of this. Aren’t there probably spaces or gimmicks that only an Inult can get into?”
“As for gimmicks, let’s just say everyone can fudge their way through somehow, no?”

“True enough. But the biggest problem is… doesn’t it seem likely there’ll be some kind of item hidden in a secret room along the way, and if we don’t collect it before reaching the 100th floor, we won’t be able to return to normal?”
At Father’s words, both Itsuki and Ren fell silent together.
“That does seem like the sort of gimmick they’d include, doesn’t it. A place where half-baked game knowledge is technically useful but inefficient—that kind of spot.”
“In the end, it doesn’t change the fact that this is basically a first-time experience for us.”
“Let’s just be careful, and if we find something that looks the part, examine it thoroughly.”
“Yeah… turning into a monster and adventuring to get back to your original form—that’s a theme I’ve seen scattered around in old games, now that I think about it.”
“Naofumi-san doesn’t seem to know of a game similar to this world, but he does seem to have knowledge of other games, doesn’t he.”
That’s certainly true. I feel like Father has more knowledge about things I don’t know, in situations like this.

“Well, sure. Simply put, in a game about clearing a tower, there’s one where—not monsters, but a knight—collects items inside a tower, defeats the boss at the top floor, and rescues the captured girl along with the treasure. That kind of thing comes up first. There was an item you’d absolutely never find on a first playthrough without prior knowledge.”
“Given our current situation, that doesn’t sound like a joke at all, so I’ll ask just for reference—what kind of item?”
“Like defeating a specific monster, or hitting a wall a certain number of times, or blocking a set number of monster attacks, or moving from the top of the screen to the bottom.”
Right as Father was explaining this, Ren and Itsuki both covered their ears.
“Naofumi, read the room! Do you have any idea how long we’d have to stay like this if we were in that kind of situation?”
“Exactly! Motoyasu-san is more than enough to handle that kind of trial-and-error business alone!”
Why is my name coming up here, I wonder? Should Father command it, this Motoyasu shall accomplish the task even without Ren and Itsuki, I say.
“True, if we leave it to Motoyasu-kun, he’d probably do it no matter how long it took.”
“Leave it to me, indeed.”
“Meanwhile the rest of us would spend that time as pets. I doubt we’d ever return to normal within our lifetimes.”
“Anyway, let’s scrap this possibility. Got any other knowledge?”

“Feels like our positions have somehow reversed here, but—there was also a simple arcade game where you climb a tower collecting ingredients for a medicine to turn back to normal. The characters later reappeared in a puzzle game, too.”
Father really is knowledgeable about all sorts of games. I thought I’d played quite a lot myself, but knowing Father makes me keenly aware I was still just a beginner at best.
“This one sounds more like our situation.”
“Well, in that case, if you can reach the top floor in a single attempt, there’s no leftover items—so if you’re skilled, you end up with everything you need.”
“So we’re pinning our hopes on the boss, then. If we find something that looks the part, let’s give up on any temporary return trips.”
“There’s also a game where you turn into a monster and travel the world to break a curse, but that’s a bit different, so don’t worry about it.”
“Still… I’m not sure if it’s limited to just Naofumi-san’s world, but Japanese games really do have all sorts of situations, don’t they.”
Itsuki’s opinion is a fair one. There are plenty of games I don’t know either.
“Either way, I suppose we’ve got no choice but to search carefully as we go.”
“Getting back to the topic—Ren-san’s got smell, I’ve got wall-climbing or tree-climbing, Naofumi-san’s got swimming, so what would Motoyasu-san have?”
“It’d have to be some kind of Usauni trait, I guess.”
At this, I gave my ears a little twitch, showing off.
“With these Usauni Motoyasu Ears, I can distinguish any sound whatsoever, I say.”
“I won’t deny you’ve got sharp hearing, but we’re talking about gimmicks Motoyasu-san might be able to pull off for dungeon-clearing here.”
“It does seem like he’d use his ears like a whip to move around, but that’s not it either. The safe bet would probably be something like being fast on his feet… or digging into the ground, maybe?”
“Digging seems like an ability that isn’t exclusive to Peckuls, though.”
Indeed, dogs, squirrels, and rabbits are all creatures with a habit of digging into the ground.
“Then jumping power?”
“He already proved he could fly earlier, remember?”
“Well, aside from jumping, if we’re talking Usauni traits, wouldn’t it be speed on foot? Like… quickly moving through places with time limits, that sort of feel.”
“If there’s some game-like gimmick in that area, that’d be the safe assumption, I suppose.”
Indeed, I feel very light on my feet right now. I have confidence in both my speed of movement and my jumping ability, I say.
“Somehow it’s really annoying how Motoyasu-san keeps striking poses over every little thing.”
“Let’s try not to dwell on that too much… ah, right, sounds—there’s probably also something like hitting walls to find hollow spaces.”
“Discovering hidden items that can’t be found by smell, huh. That does seem likely.”
“Motoyasu-kun. Try tapping on walls periodically as we go, without breaking them.”
“Understood, indeed.”

And so, as we made our way forward like this… on the way to the 3rd floor, there was a mural. On it was what appeared to be an Inult, depicted sniffing out and obtaining an item. Ren, seizing the moment, declared he smelled something strange, examined the wall, and found a hidden tool—an Oreikal ore used for weapon enhancement.
“Wow, what a blatant tutorial.”
“It’s so thoughtful I could cry.”
“The people who made this place are definitely having fun with us.”
“Shouldn’t we appreciate the fact that it hasn’t been destroyed, though? Considering everything so far, it seems like without Motoyasu-kun and the others, we’d have had almost no hints at all.”
“True enough… this must mean this labyrinth isn’t connected to the mastermind behind the Waves, then.”
“Hope we find some kind of nice reward for clearing it.”
“So, the next mural is… just as expected, Risuka’s thing seems to be wall-climbing.”
There was a mural depicting Risuka climbing up a wall. Oh? It looks like she can cling to ceilings too.

“So she can act on ceilings as well… it’s different from flying, but she can move freely in all directions. In an action game, Itsuki’d probably be the type with a hook-shot gun or bow to secure mobility, right?”
“Even if I’m the only one who can get there… well, if there’s an item beyond that spot, I’ll have no choice but to do it.”
“What she can do sounds like the same kind of movement as a playable slime character.”
“Ah… true, that does seem like the kind of movement she could pull off.”
“Father. There’s a more familiar creature for this, I say. One that moves along walls and ceilings—Itsuki should have wings and antennae attached and be painted black, indeed.”
“I’ll take you up on that fight! Who are you calling a mental parasite!”
An Itsuki who gets carried away brandishing justice is no different from a mental parasite, I say.
“Now, now…”
“What exactly are ‘Frontier Creatures’ supposed to be, anyway…”
And so, defeating the monsters that appeared as we advanced… this time, there was a mural of a Usauni. It was digging into the ground.
